claim: Leg motoneurons in Drosophila are organized as a myotopic map, where their dendritic domains represent the muscle field.
source: In Drosophila, leg motoneurons are organized as a myotopic map, where their dendritic domains represent the muscle field.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract as a known fact about Drosophila leg motoneurons.

claim: A behavioral screen identified roles for Semaphorins (Sema) and Plexins (Plex) in walking behavior.
source: A behavioral screen identified roles for Semaphorins (Sema) and Plexins (Plex) in walking behavior.
evidence: The authors report conducting a behavioral screen that identified these roles, as described in the abstract and Results section.

claim: PlexA/Sema1a mediates motoneuron axon branching in ways that differ in the proximal femur and distal tibia, based on motoneuronal birth order.
source: Deciphering this phenotype, we show that PlexA/Sema1a mediates motoneuron axon branching in ways that differ in the proximal femur and distal tibia, based on motoneuronal birth order.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the Results section.

claim: PlexB/Sema2a is required for dendritic positioning of late-born motoneurons but not early-born motoneurons.
source: Importantly, we show a novel role for glia in positioning dendrites of specific motoneurons; PlexB/Sema2a is required for dendritic positioning of late-born motoneurons but not early-born motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported in the abstract and supported by experimental data in the Results section.

claim: Glia play a novel role in positioning dendrites of specific motoneurons.
source: Importantly, we show a novel role for glia in positioning dendrites of specific motoneurons
evidence: This is stated as a novel finding in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing Sema2a knockdown in glial cells affects dendritic positioning.

claim: Communication within motoneurons and between glia and motoneurons, mediated by the combined action of different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems, are required for the formation of a functional myotopic map.
source: These findings indicate that communication within motoneurons and between glia and motoneurons, mediated by the combined action of different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems, are required for the formation of a functional myotopic map.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract, synthesizing the experimental findings.

claim: Motoneurons represent the final common path for convergence of processed information from motor control circuitry in the central nervous system and from sensory feedback circuitry in the periphery.
source: They represent the final common path for convergence of processed information from motor control circuitry in the central nervous system and from sensory feedback circuitry in the periphery (Sherrington, 1906; Pearson, 1993).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Motoneurons represent exclusive control elements of muscle effectors that mediate behavioral action.
source: Moreover, as final common output channels, they represent exclusive control elements of muscle effectors that mediate behavioral action.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the Introduction.

claim: The majority of leg motoneurons are postembryonic lineal descendants of neuroblast 15.
source: For example, the specific architecture of the motoneurons that innervate the adult leg has been shown to depend on their lineage and birth order, in that the majority of the leg motoneurons are postembryonic lineal descendants of neuroblast 15, and these motoneurons manifest a birth order-specific neuroanatomical organization (Truman et al., 2004; Brierley et al., 2009; Brierley et al., 2012; Baek and Mann, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Early born motoneurons project their axons to proximal muscles in the leg segments and have dendritic arborization that extends toward the thoracic ganglion neuropile midline.
source: In this lineage, early born motoneurons project their axons to proximal muscles in the leg segments and have dendritic arborization that extends toward the thoracic ganglion neuropile midline
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about leg motoneuron organization.

claim: Late born motoneurons innervate distal muscles in the leg segments and have dendritic arbors that are restricted to the lateral regions of the ganglionic neuropile.
source: whereas late born motoneurons innervate distal muscles in the leg segments and have dendritic arbors that are restricted to the lateral regions of the ganglionic neuropile.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about leg motoneuron organization.

claim: Leg motoneurons form a myotopic map in terms of their central and peripheral nervous architecture.
source: Thus, in terms of their central and peripheral nervous architecture, these leg motoneurons form a myotopic map (Brierley et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: Myotopic map-specific targeting of leg motoneuron dendrites requires midline signaling through the Slit/Roundabout and Netrin/Frazzled signaling systems.
source: Although this myotopic map-specific targeting of leg motoneuron dendrites has been shown to require midline signaling through the Slit/Roundabout and Netrin/Frazzled signaling systems (Brierley et al., 2009), the mechanism underlying compartmentalization in terms of birth order and distinct axonal and dendritic targeting is poorly understood.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with a supporting citation.

claim: PlexinA (PlexA) strongly binds the Sema1a and Sema1b ligands.
source: PlexinA (PlexA) strongly binds the Sema1a and Sema1b ligands while as Plexin B (PlexB) binds to Sema2a and Sema2b (Bates and Whitington, 2007; Ayoob et al., 2006; Lattemann et al., 2007; Sweeney et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Plexin B (PlexB) binds to Sema2a and Sema2b.
source: PlexinA (PlexA) strongly binds the Sema1a and Sema1b ligands while as Plexin B (PlexB) binds to Sema2a and Sema2b (Bates and Whitington, 2007; Ayoob et al., 2006; Lattemann et al., 2007; Sweeney et al., 2011)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Both PlexA and PlexB have been shown to mediate a Sema-dependent repulsion of motor axons during embryonic development of body wall innervation.
source: Both PlexA and PlexB have been shown to mediate a Sema-dependent repulsion of motor axons during embryonic development of body wall innervation (Winberg et al., 1998; Yu et al., 1998; Jeong et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The OK371-Gal4 driver targets reporter gene expression to all motoneurons during embryonic and postembryonic development and in the adult.
source: In these experiments, the OK371-Gal4 driver was used to target UAS-RNAi knockdown to leg motoneurons; this Gal4 driver targets reporter gene expression to all motoneurons during embryonic and postembryonic development and in the adult (Mahr and Aberle, 2006; Brierley et al., 2009; Brierley et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the Gal4 driver with supporting citations.

claim: Locomotor defects were observed in RNAi-mediated knockdown of Sema1a, PlexA, and PlexB in leg motoneurons.
source: Locomotor defects were observed in RNAi-mediated knockdown of Sema1a, PlexA, and PlexB in leg motoneurons (Figure 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1.

claim: In Sema1a knockdown experiments, flies showed uncoordinated walking activity with leg dragging.
source: In Sema1a knockdown experiments, flies showed uncoordinated walking activity with leg dragging.
evidence: This is a specific behavioral phenotype observed in the experiments.

claim: In PlexA knockdown experiments, flies showed uncoordinated walking, short steps or short steps with leg dragging.
source: In PlexA knockdown experiments, flies showed uncoordinated walking, short steps or short steps with leg dragging.
evidence: This is a specific behavioral phenotype observed in the experiments.

claim: In PlexB knockdown experiments, flies walked with short steps and leg dragging.
source: In PlexB knockdown experiments, flies walked with short steps and leg dragging.
evidence: This is a specific behavioral phenotype observed in the experiments.

claim: In Sema2a knockdown experiments, flies showed normal walking behavior.
source: In Sema2a knockdown experiments, flies showed normal walking behavior.
evidence: This is a specific behavioral observation from the experiments.

claim: PlexA, PlexB, and Sema1a, but not Sema2a, are required in leg motoneurons during development and/or in the adult for the manifestation of correct locomotor activity.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that PlexA, PlexB, and Sema1a, but not Sema2a, are required in leg motoneurons during development and/or in the adult for the manifestation of correct locomotor activity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the behavioral screen data.

claim: In the wild-type femur, the proximal axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve and innervates the ltm2 (long tendon muscle 2).
source: In the wild-type femur, the proximal axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve and innervates the ltm2 (long tendon muscle 2), while as another axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve more distally, projects further distally and innervates the tidm (tibia depressor muscle) (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This describes the normal anatomy observed in control experiments, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Another axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve more distally, projects further distally and innervates the tidm (tibia depressor muscle) in the wild-type femur.
source: In the wild-type femur, the proximal axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve and innervates the ltm2 (long tendon muscle 2), while as another axon branch defasciculates from the main motor nerve more distally, projects further distally and innervates the tidm (tibia depressor muscle) (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: This describes the normal anatomy observed in control experiments, shown in Figure 2.

claim: Following targeted knockdown of either PlexA or Sema1a, axon projection defects were seen in the proximal femur.
source: Following targeted knockdown of either PlexA or Sema1a, axon projection defects were seen in the proximal femur; for both PlexA and Sema1a knockdowns two similar kinds of projection phenotypes were observed either separately or in combination (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in figures.

claim: In PlexA or Sema1a knockdown, the axon branch that normally innervates the tidm defasciculates from the main motor nerve correctly, but then stalls and does not project distally along the femur to innervate the tidm correctly.
source: In the first phenotype, the axon branch that normally innervates the tidm defasciculates from the main motor nerve correctly, but then stalls and does not project distally along the femur to innervate the tidm correctly (Figure 2E–H).
evidence: This describes a specific axon projection defect observed in knockdown experiments, shown in Figure 2.

claim: In PlexA or Sema1a knockdown, the axon branch that normally innervates ltm2 fails to defasciculate and exit from the main motor nerve and innervation of the ltm2 is lacking.
source: In the second phenotype, the axon branch that normally innervates ltm2 fails to defasciculate and exit from the main motor nerve and innervation of the ltm2 is lacking (Figure 2I–L).
evidence: This describes a specific axon projection defect observed in knockdown experiments, shown in Figure 2.

claim: In the distal wild-type tibia, several axon branches defasciculate from the main motor nerve to innervate the tadm (tarsus depressor muscle) and two terminal branches defasciculate from the main motor nerve to innervate the tarm (tarsus reductor muscle).
source: In the distal wild-type tibia, several axon branches defasciculate from the main motor nerve to innervate the tadm (tarsus depressor muscle) and two terminal branches defasciculate from the main motor nerve to innervate the tarm (tarsus reductor muscle) (Figure 3A–D).
evidence: This describes the normal anatomy observed in control experiments, shown in Figure 3.

claim: After targeted knockdown of PlexA, axon projection defects characterized by a marked increase in the number of axon branches that exit the main nerve resulted in the distal tibia.
source: After targeted knockdown of PlexA, axon projection defects characterized by a marked increase in the number of axon branches that exit the main nerve resulted (Figure 3 E-H).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: The increase in axon branches after PlexA knockdown was seen both in the axon branches that innervate the tadm and in the axon branches that innervate the tarm.
source: This increase was seen both in the axon branches that innervate the tadm and in the axon branches that innervate the tarm.
evidence: This describes the specific nature of the axon projection defect observed.

claim: A comparable increase in the number of axon branches that exit the main nerve resulted after targeted knockdown of Sema1a in the distal tibia.
source: A comparable increase in the number of axon branches that exit the main nerve resulted after targeted knockdown of Sema1a; however, this was usually more pronounced in the axon branches that innervate tarm (Figure 3I–L; Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: An abnormal reduction of PlexA/Sema1a in all leg motoneurons can lead to defective axonal branching phenotypes.
source: Taken together, these findings indicate that an abnormal reduction of PlexA/Sema1a in all leg motoneurons can lead to defective axonal branching phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the knockdown experiments.

claim: The observed phenotypes differ in the proximal femur and the distal tibia in that a reduction in axon branching of motoneurons occurs in the femur and an increase in axon branching of motoneurons occurs in the tibia.
source: The observed phenotypes differ in the proximal femur and the distal tibia in that a reduction in axon branching of motoneurons occurs in the femur and an increase in axon branching of motoneurons occurs in the tibia.
evidence: This is a summary of the differential effects observed in different leg segments.

claim: Targeted overexpression of Sema1a in leg motoneurons resulted in an increase in axon branching in the proximal femur characterized by excessive defasciculation and ectopic branches exiting the main motor nerve in all preparations analyzed.
source: In the proximal femur, targeted overexpression of Sema1a in leg motoneurons resulted in an increase in axon branching that was characterized by excessive defasciculation and ectopic branches exiting the main motor nerve in all preparations analyzed (Figure 2M–P).
evidence: This is a primary finding from overexpression experiments shown in Figure 2.

claim: Extensive defasciculation following Sema1a overexpression was accompanied by a correspondingly reduced thickness of the nerve's main axon bundle.
source: Moreover, this extensive defasciculation was accompanied by a correspondingly reduced thickness of the nerve's main axon bundle (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the overexpression experiments shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Comparable defasciculation phenotypes were observed in targeted PlexA overexpression experiments in the proximal femur.
source: Comparable defasciculation phenotypes were observed in targeted PlexA overexpression experiments (Figure 2Q–T; Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments shown in figures.

claim: In most cases, PlexA overexpression defasciculation phenotypes were less extensive than in the Sema1a overexpression experiments, and a marked reduction of thickness in the main axon bundle of the nerve was usually not seen.
source: However, in most cases, these defasciculation phenotypes were less extensive than in the Sema1a overexpression experiments, and a marked reduction of thickness in the main axon bundle of the nerve was usually not seen (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a comparative observation from the overexpression experiments.

claim: Targeted overexpression of PlexA in leg motoneurons resulted in a decrease in axon branching in the distal tibia characterized by a striking reduction in the number of axon branches that exit the main motor nerve and innervate the tadm and tarm.
source: In the distal tibia, targeted overexpression of PlexA in leg motoneurons resulted in a decrease in axon branching that was characterized by a striking reduction in the number of axon branches that exit the main motor nerve and innervate the tadm and tarm (Figure 3Q–T).
evidence: This is a primary finding from overexpression experiments shown in Figure 3.

claim: Targeted overexpression of Sema1a also resulted in reduced defasciculation and branching phenotypes in several cases in the distal tibia; however, these were less extensive than in the PlexA overexpression experiments.
source: Targeted overexpression of Sema1a also resulted in reduced defasciculation and branching phenotypes in several cases; however, these were less extensive than in the PlexA overexpression experiments (Figure 3M–P; Figure 3—figure supplement 1D; Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from overexpression experiments shown in figures.

claim: Both reduction and increase of PlexA/Sema1a expression in motoneurons can result in aberrant axonal branch formation in the proximal muscles of the femur and in the distal muscles of the tibia.
source: Thus, both reduction and increase of PlexA/Sema1a expression in motoneurons can result in aberrant axonal branch formation in the proximal muscles of the femur and in the distal muscles of the tibia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from both knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: Reduction and increase in PlexA/Sema1a expression result in opposing branching phenotypes.
source: Moreover, reduction and increase in PlexA/Sema1a expression result in opposing branching phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: A normal level of PlexA/Sema1a-mediated signaling is required in leg motoneurons for the formation of correct axonal projections and targeted muscle innervation in the leg.
source: Taken together, these experiments indicate that a normal level of PlexA/Sema1a-mediated signaling is required in leg motoneurons for the formation of correct axonal projections and targeted muscle innervation in the leg.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined knockdown and overexpression experiments.

claim: The VGN6341-Gal4 driver targets knockdowns to 3–4 motoneurons that innervate the femur as well as 1–2 motoneurons that innervate the tibia.
source: To investigate this possibility, we used the VGN6341-Gal4 driver which targets knockdowns to 3–4 motoneurons that innervate the femur as well as 1–2 motoneurons that innervate the tibia.
evidence: This describes the specificity of the Gal4 driver used in experiments.

claim: In the wild type, femur motoneurons labeled by VGN6341-Gal4 always innervated the tidm and ltm2 muscles of the proximal femur.
source: In the wild type, femur motoneurons labeled by VGN6341-Gal4 always innervated the tidm and ltm2 muscles of the proximal femur and, similarly, tibia motoneurons always innervated the tadm muscles of the distal tibia.
evidence: This describes the normal innervation pattern observed in control experiments.

claim: Following targeted knockdown of PlexA and Sema1a using VGN6341-Gal4, motoneurons that normally innervated the femur manifested a significant number of mis-projection phenotypes characterized by lack of innervation of the tidm and ltm2 muscles of the femur and ectopic innervation of the ltm1 and tidm muscles of the tibia.
source: In contrast, following targeted knockdown of PlexA and Sema1a, motoneurons that normally innervated the femur manifested a significant number of mis-projection phenotypes characterized by lack of innervation of the tidm and ltm2 muscles of the femur and ectopic innervation of the ltm1 and tidm muscles of the tibia.
evidence: This is a primary finding from targeted knockdown experiments using a specific Gal4 driver.

claim: Comparable mis-projection phenotypes were seen in femur motoneurons in a Sema1a homozygous null mutant, Sema1a heteroallelic combination and in animals trans-heterozygous for mutants in both Sema1a and PlexA of the genotype Sema1aP2/+;;PlexA09/+.
source: Comparable mis-projection phenotypes were seen in these femur motoneurons in a Sema1a homozygous null mutant, Sema1a hetreroallelic combination and in animals trans-heterozygous for mutants in both Sema1a and PlexA of the genotype Sema1aP2/+;;PlexA09/+.
evidence: This is a finding from genetic mutant analysis shown in Figure 4.

claim: A reduction of PlexA/Sema1a in motoneurons that normally innervate the femur can result in a loss of appropriate femoral innervation and a gain of inappropriate tibial innervation.
source: Taken together, these findings imply that a reduction of PlexA/Sema1a in motoneurons that normally innervate the femur can result in a loss of appropriate femoral innervation and a gain of inappropriate tibial innervation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the targeted knockdown experiments using VGN6341-Gal4.

claim: These specific mis-projection phenotypes of femur motoneurons are likely to contribute to the observed overall axonal projection phenotype in the leg, characterized by decreased axonal branching in the femur and increased axonal branching in the tibia.
source: These specific mis-projection phenotypes of femur motoneurons are likely to contribute to the observed overall axonal projection phenotype in the leg, characterized by decreased axonal branching in the femur and increased axonal branching in the tibia.
evidence: This is an inference connecting the specific mis-projection phenotypes to the overall phenotype.

claim: Throughout postembryonic development, both Sema1a and Sema2a are widely expressed throughout most of the developing thoracic ganglia.
source: Throughout postembryonic development, both Sema1a and Sema2a are widely expressed throughout most of the developing thoracic ganglia (Figure 5A–F).
evidence: This is an observation from immunolabeling experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Sema1a and Sema2a expression levels are significantly different at the ganglionic midline.
source: However, Sema1a and Sema2a expression levels are significantly different at the ganglionic midline.
evidence: This is an observation from immunolabeling experiments.

claim: Sema1a expression decreases toward the midline and has its lowest level of expression there.
source: Thus, whereas Sema1a expression decreases toward the midline and has its lowest level of expression there, Sema2a expression is highest at/and near midline where a peak in its expression level is manifest (Figure 5G–H; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from immunolabeling experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: Sema2a expression is highest at/and near midline where a peak in its expression level is manifest.
source: Thus, whereas Sema1a expression decreases toward the midline and has its lowest level of expression there, Sema2a expression is highest at/and near midline where a peak in its expression level is manifest (Figure 5G–H; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from immunolabeling experiments shown in Figure 5.

claim: The high level of Sema2a expression in and around midline cells, many of which are glial in nature, suggests that Sema2a ligand secreted from these cells could affect leg motoneuron development within the thoracic ganglia and hence, influence the pattern of dendrite outgrowth in leg motoneurons in a non-cell autonomous manner.
source: This high level of expression in and around midline cells, many of which are glial in nature, suggests that Sema2a ligand secreted from these cells could affect leg motoneuron development within the thoracic ganglia and hence, influence the pattern of dendrite outgrowth in leg motoneurons in a non-cell autonomous manner.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the expression pattern observed.

claim: Dye backfilling of leg nerve from proximal muscles of femur labeled early-born motoneurons while backfilling the leg nerve from distal muscles of the tibia labeled late-born motoneurons.
source: Dye backfilling of leg nerve from proximal muscles of femur labeled early-born motoneurons while backfilling the leg nerve from distal muscles of the tibia labeled late-born motoneurons (Figure 6A–D).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used to label different motoneuron populations.

claim: In the wild type, early-born motoneurons have dendrites that arborize primarily in the ipsilateral neuropile, but also project one prominent branch to the ganglionic midline.
source: In the wild type, early-born motoneurons have dendrites that arborize primarily in the ipsilateral neuropile, but also project one prominent branch to the ganglionic midline (Figure 6C).
evidence: This describes the normal dendritic morphology observed in control experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Wild-type late-born motoneurons have dendrites whose arborizations are restricted to lateral part of the ipsilateral neuropile; none of their dendrites project medially.
source: In contrast, wild-type late-born motoneurons have dendrites whose arborizations are restricted to lateral part of the ipsilateral neuropile; none of their dendrites project medially (Figure 6D).
evidence: This describes the normal dendritic morphology observed in control experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: RNAi knockdown of PlexB in motoneurons using the OK371-Gal4 driver resulted in a marked dendritic arborization phenotype in the late-born motoneurons but not in the early born motoneurons.
source: RNAi knockdown of PlexB in motoneurons using the OK371-Gal4 driver resulted in a marked dendritic arborization phenotype in the late-born motoneurons but not in the early born motoneurons (Figure 6E,F).
evidence: This is a primary finding from knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: The PlexB knockdown phenotype in late-born motoneurons was characterized by a shift of the dendritic arborizations toward the midline as well as by the formation of a prominent ectopic dendritic branch, which projects to the ganglionic midline.
source: This phenotype was characterized by a shift of the dendritic arborizations toward the midline as well as by the formation of a prominent ectopic dendritic branch, which projects to the ganglionic midline.
evidence: This describes the specific dendritic phenotype observed in PlexB knockdown experiments.

claim: Late-born neurons in the PlexB knockdown experiment resemble early-born neurons in the wild type.
source: In this respect, late-born neurons in the knockdown experiment resemble early-born neurons in the wild type.
evidence: This is an observation comparing the phenotype to wild-type morphology.

claim: Targeted knockdown of Sema2a in leg motoneurons using the OK371-Gal4 driver had no effect on dendritic arbors of late-born or early-born motoneurons.
source: Targeted knockdown of Sema2a in leg motoneurons using the OK371-Gal4 driver had no effect on dendritic arbors of late-born or early-born motoneurons (data not shown).
evidence: This is a negative result from knockdown experiments.

claim: Sema2a knockdown in glial cells using either the glial-specific Repo-Gal4 driver or the midline-specific Slit-Gal4 driver resulted in clear dendritic arborization defects of leg motoneurons.
source: In both cases, Sema2a knockdown resulted in clear dendritic arborization defects of leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding from targeted knockdown experiments in glial cells.

claim: Sema2a knockdown in glial cells resulted in dendritic defects that were observed in late-born motoneurons but not in early-born motoneurons.
source: Moreover, these defects were observed in late-born motoneurons but not in early-born motoneurons.
evidence: This describes the specificity of the dendritic defects observed.

claim: Following targeted knockdown of Sema2a in glial cells, late-born motoneurons, which normally restrict their dendritic arbors to lateral domains, shift their dendritic arbors medially and mis-project major dendritic branches toward the ganglionic midline.
source: Thus, following targeted knockdown of Sema2a in glial cells, late-born motoneurons, which normally restrict their dendritic arbors to lateral domains, shift their dendritic arbors medially and mis-project major dendritic branches toward the ganglionic midline (Figure 6G,H; Figure 6—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a primary finding from targeted knockdown experiments shown in Figure 6.

claim: Comparable mis-projection phenotypes were seen in dendrites of late born motoneurons in animals of the genotype Sema2a/+; PlexB/+.
source: Comparable mis-projection phenotypes were seen in dendrites of late born motoneurons in animals of the genotype Sema2a/+; PlexB/+ (Figure 6—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from genetic mutant analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: Upon dendritic mis-projection in late-born motoneurons, dendritic arborizations of these motoneurons acquired morphological characteristics of arborizations of normal early born neurons.
source: Upon this dendritic mis-projection in late-born motoneurons, dendritic arborizations of these motoneurons acquired morphological characteristics of arborizations of normal early born neurons.
evidence: This is an observation about the phenotype resulting from Sema2a knockdown in glial cells.

claim: PlexB/Sema2a signaling is required for the formation of correct dendritic projections of late-born leg motoneurons.
source: Taken together these experiments indicate that PlexB/Sema2a signaling is required for the formation of correct dendritic projections of late-born leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the knockdown experiments.

claim: The requirement for PlexB in late-born motoneurons is cell autonomous and the requirement for Sema2a is non-cell autonomous (i.e. glial/midline cell-derived).
source: Moreover, they imply that the requirement in these motoneurons is cell autonomous for PlexB and non-cell autonomous (i.e. glial/midline cell-derived) for Sema2a.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing motoneuron-specific and glial-specific knockdown experiments.

claim: PlexA/Sema1a is required for correct peripheral axon guidance, and for both PlexA and Sema1a this requirement is motoneuron-specific.
source: PlexA/Sema1a is required for correct peripheral axon guidance, and for both PlexA and Sema1a this requirement is motoneuron-specific.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the axon guidance experiments.

claim: PlexB/Sema2a is required for correct central dendrite targeting.
source: PlexB/Sema2a is required for correct central dendrite targeting, and while this requirement is motoneuron-specific for PlexB, the requirement for Sema2a in motoneurons is non-cell autonomous and likely involves glial cells.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the dendrite targeting experiments.

claim: While PlexA/Sema1a appears to be required for both early-born and late-born motoneuron axon guidance, PlexB/Sema2a appears to be required for late-born, but not for early-born motoneuron dendritic patterning.
source: Interestingly, while PlexA/Sema1a appears to be required for both early-born and late-born motoneuron axon guidance, PlexB/Sema2a appears to be required for late-born, but not for early-born motoneuron dendritic patterning.
evidence: This is a summary of the differential requirements observed in the experiments.

claim: Both peripheral axonal outgrowth and central dendritic targeting of leg motoneurons occur at the same/overlapping times during postembryonic development.
source: This seems unlikely as timeline analysis indicates that both peripheral axonal outgrowth and central dendritic targeting of leg motoneurons occur at the same/overlapping times during postembryonic development (Brierley et al., 2009; 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Specific experimental perturbations in the expression levels of the Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems result in abnormal walking behavior.
source: Our behavioral experiments indicate that specific experimental perturbations in the expression levels of the Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems result in abnormal walking behavior.
evidence: This is a summary of the behavioral screen results.

claim: The same molecular perturbations that result in abnormal walking behavior also result in defective axonal and dendritic branching and arborization patterns in leg motoneurons.
source: Moreover, they show that the same molecular perturbations also result in defective axonal and dendritic branching and arborization patterns in leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is a summary connecting behavioral and anatomical phenotypes.

claim: The striking correlation between perturbation in leg motoneuron architecture and defective walking behavior provides further support for the idea that peripheral and central architecture is likely to be important for the function of the motoneurons involved in the neural circuitry for walking.
source: Although other effects of the Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems on the neural circuitry for walking control may exist, the striking correlation between perturbation in leg motoneuron architecture and defective walking behavior provides further support for the idea that peripheral and central architecture is likely to be important for the function of the motoneurons involved in the neural circuitry for walking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation between behavioral and anatomical phenotypes.

claim: Dendritic targeting in larval motoneurons is an active process that is independent of glial differentiation or target muscle formation.
source: The dendritic targeting of larval motoneurons is an active process that is independent of glial differentiation or target muscle formation (Landgraf et al., 2003; Landgraf and Thor, 2006).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Glia play a role in positioning dendrites of late born motoneurons that innervate distal muscles of tibia and occupy lateral regions of the thoracic neuropil in adult Drosophila.
source: In contrast, we find the role of glia in positioning dendrites of late born motoneurons that innervate distal muscles of tibia and occupy lateral regions of the thoracic neuropil in adult Drosophila.
evidence: This is a primary finding that contrasts with larval motoneurons.

claim: Motoneuron-specific knockdown of PlexB or knockdown of Sema2a secreted from glial cells results in a shift of dendritic arborization toward the ganglionic midline in late born leg motoneurons.
source: We demonstrate that motoneuron-specific knockdown of PlexB or knockdown of Sema2a secreted from glial cells results in a shift of dendritic arborization toward the ganglionic midline in late born leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is a primary finding from the knockdown experiments.

claim: The integrative action of multiple Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems mediate communication between glia and motoneurons and within motoneurons for the correct formation of axonal projections and dendritic arborization in leg motoneuron development.
source: These findings indicate that the integrative action of multiple Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems mediate communication between glia and motoneurons and within motoneurons for the correct formation of axonal projections and dendritic arborization in leg motoneuron development.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the Results section.

claim: Sema1a acting through PlexA has been shown to be important for the regulation of motoneuron axon defasciculation through axon-axon repulsion.
source: Sema1a acting through PlexA has been shown to be important for the regulation of motoneuron axon defasciculation through axon-axon repulsion (Winberg et al., 1998; 2001; Yu et al., 1998; 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: Sema2a acting through PlexB is required for correct motoneuron axon defasciculation, but also has additional functions in motoneuron axon navigation.
source: Similarly, Sema2a acting through PlexB is required for correct motoneuron axon defasciculation, but also has additional functions in motoneuron axon navigation (Matthes et al., 1995; Ayoob et al., 2006)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: PlexA/Sema1a and PlexB/Sema2a have both shared and distinct function in motor axon guidance.
source: implying that PlexA/Sema1a and PlexB/Sema2a have both shared and distinct function in motor axon guidance.
evidence: This is an inference based on cited literature.

claim: The same Plexin/Semaphorin signaling system might have multiple roles in motor axon guidance.
source: These findings suggest that the same Plexin/Semaphorin signaling system might have multiple roles in motor axon guidance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation of different phenotypes in different leg segments.

claim: The different effects of PlexA/Sema1a appear to be motoneuron-specific and may be linked to motoneuron birth-order.
source: Since these different effects appear to be motoneuron-specific, they may be linked to motoneuron birth-order.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the observed phenotypes.

claim: The requirement of both PlexA and Sema1 for correct axonal targeting is autonomous to leg motoneurons.
source: In this respect, the requirement of both PlexA and Sema1 for correct axonal targeting is autonomous to leg motoneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the motoneuron-specific knockdown experiments.

claim: PlexA/Sema1a signaling might be at the level of axon-axon interactions.
source: This suggests that PlexA/Sema1a signaling might be at the level of axon-axon interactions.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the autonomous requirement in motoneurons.

claim: Cis-interactions between PlexA and Sema1a within the affected motoneuron axons might also be involved.
source: Alternatively, cis-interactions between PlexA and Sema1a within the affected motoneuron axons might also be involved.
evidence: This is an alternative hypothesis proposed by the authors.

claim: In murine models, cis-interactions between Sema6A and PlexA4 have been shown to modulate the repulsive response to Sema6A in sympathetic and sensory neurons.
source: In murine models, cis- interactions between Sema6A and PlexA4 have been shown to modulate the repulsive response to Sema6A in sympathetic and sensory neurons (Haklai-Topper et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge from vertebrate studies with a supporting citation.

claim: Leg motoneuron dendrites are organized topographically as myotopic maps that reflect their innervation pattern in the periphery.
source: Although the mechanisms that control this type of targeted dendritogenesis are poorly understood, recent work on embryonic and adult-specific leg motoneurons in Drosophila indicate that their dendrites are organized topographically as myotopic maps that reflect their innervation pattern in the periphery (Landgraf et al., 2003; Brierley et al., 2012; 2009; Baek and Mann, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: A birth-order dependent pattern of dendritic targeting and of peripheral innervation has been documented for leg motoneurons.
source: For leg motoneurons, the majority of which are generated post-embryonically in a single neuroblast lineage, a birth-order dependent pattern of dendritic targeting and of peripheral innervation has been documented (Brierley et al., 2009; 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: All leg motoneurons initiate dendritogenesis synchronously and form their dendritic arbors in a targeted manner by growing into their appropriate area of innervation.
source: Irrespective of their birth-order, all leg motoneurons initiate dendritogenesis synchronously and form their dendritic arbors in a targeted manner by growing into their appropriate area of innervation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about leg motoneuron development.

claim: Leg motoneuron dendrites attain their final architecture through targeted dendritogenesis.
source: Leg motoneuron dendrites attain their final architecture through targeted dendritogenesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about leg motoneuron development.

claim: Glia are known to secrete cues and neurotropic factors for axonal morphogenesis and survival.
source: Although glia are known to secrete cues and neurotropic factors for axonal morphogenesis and survival (Jacobs, 2000; Martin et al., 2012; Zlatic et al., 2009; Klämbt et al., 1991), their role in regulation of dendritic morphology is relatively unexplored.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with supporting citations.

claim: The role of glia in regulation of dendritic morphology is relatively unexplored.
source: Although glia are known to secrete cues and neurotropic factors for axonal morphogenesis and survival (Jacobs, 2000; Martin et al., 2012; Zlatic et al., 2009; Klämbt et al., 1991), their role in regulation of dendritic morphology is relatively unexplored.
evidence: This is stated as a gap in current knowledge.

claim: Sema2a is secreted from midline and other glial cells and acts through the PlexB receptor to restrict dendrites of late-born motoneurons to appropriate lateral neuropile domains.
source: Our data are in accordance with a model in which Sema2a is secreted from midline and other glial cells and acts through the PlexB receptor to restrict dendrites of late-born motoneurons to appropriate lateral neuropile domains.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the experimental findings.

claim: Loss of PlexB in late-born motoneurons as well as loss of Sema2a from glial cells results in a medial shift in dendritic arbors together with the mis-projection of dendrites toward the midline.
source: Loss of PlexB in these motoneurons as well as loss of Sema2a from glial cells, as seen by using both Repo-Gal4 and Slit-Gal4 drivers, results in a medial shift in dendritic arbors together with the mis-projection of dendrites toward the midline.
evidence: This is a summary of the dendritic phenotypes observed in knockdown experiments.

claim: Glial cells provide the secreted Sema2a, which acts on dendrite targeting in late-born motoneurons.
source: Since cells at/and near the ganglionic midline express high levels of Sema2a, and since targeted knockdown of Sema 2a specifically in glial cells using Repo-Gal4 results in the mis-positioning of late-born motoneuron dendrites, we postulate that glial cells provide the secreted Sema2a, which acts on dendrite targeting in late-born motoneurons.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the expression pattern and knockdown experiments.

claim: While the requirement of PlexB for dendrite targeting in late-born motoneurons is cell autonomous, the requirement of Sema2a is non-cell autonomous and presumably is provided through secretion from glial cells.
source: Thus, while the requirement of PlexB for dendrite targeting in late-born motoneurons is cell autonomous, the requirement of Sema2a is non-cell autonomous and presumably is provided through secretion from glial cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing motoneuron-specific and glial-specific knockdown experiments.

claim: Two different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems act to play a range of roles in establishing the specific leg motoneuron architecture needed for appropriate motor circuitry.
source: Taken together, our findings indicate that two different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems act to play a range of roles in establishing the specific leg motoneuron architecture needed for appropriate motor circuitry.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from all the experimental findings.

claim: The relative independence of action of these two different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems in axon guidance and dendrite targeting of leg motoneurons suggests that both developmental processes could, in principle operate at separate times.
source: The relative independence of action of these two different Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems in axon guidance and dendrite targeting of leg motoneurons suggests that both developmental processes could, in principle operate at separate times.
evidence: This is a hypothesis based on the independence of the two signaling systems.

claim: The striking correlation between perturbation in leg motoneuron architecture and defective walking behavior provides further support for the idea that peripheral and central architecture is likely to be important for the function of the motoneurons involved in the neural circuitry for walking.
source: Although other effects of the Plexin/Semaphorin signaling systems on the neural circuitry for walking control may exist, the striking correlation between perturbation in leg motoneuron architecture and defective walking behavior provides further support for the idea that peripheral and central architecture is likely to be important for the function of the motoneurons involved in the neural circuitry for walking.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation between behavioral and anatomical phenotypes.
